hyperedges.label: Cross-Host Skill Variants Sharing One Pipeline Contract

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Trae host variant)
nodes.rationale: Host-specific variant of the graphify skill: identical pipeline contract but wires integration into AGENTS.md rather than CLAUDE.md, and assumes no automated subagent dispatch API.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (VS Code host variant)
nodes.rationale: Full pipeline runbook for a host without a parallel Agent/Task API, so semantic extraction is driven by hand: a subagent per chunk is dispatched manually and its JSON pasted back to disk.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Windows/PowerShell host variant)
nodes.rationale: PowerShell rendition of the same pipeline; here-strings are piped into the saved interpreter instead of shell redirects to avoid console-encoding drift (#2528).

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Subcommands can be invoked after the user deleted graphify-out/, so the interpreter sidecar must be re-resolved before any subcommand runs.

nodes.label: /graphify query Flow (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Answer from the existing graph rather than rebuilding; expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary first so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise.

nodes.label: --update and --cluster-only (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Both are non-default subcommands, so their flows live in a reference file rather than the main runbook.

nodes.label: Commit Hook and native AGENTS.md Integration
nodes.source_location: ## For the commit hook and native AGENTS.md integration

nodes.label: Honesty Rules (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Audit-trail integrity: never invent an edge, never hide cohesion behind symbols, always show token cost, and warn before rendering HTML above 5,000 nodes.

nodes.label: /graphify Usage Block
nodes.rationale: Printed verbatim and nothing else on --help/-h, so a help invocation never triggers detection or defaults the path to '.'.

nodes.label: Fast Path — Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, the graph is already built — skip Steps 1-5 and query it rather than paying for re-extraction.

nodes.label: Step 0 — GitHub Repos and Multi-Path Merge
nodes.rationale: Only runs for GitHub URLs or several local subfolders; a plain local path skips it entirely.

nodes.label: Step 1 — Ensure graphify Is Installed
nodes.rationale: Interpreter resolution is ordered uv tool -> graphify shebang -> python3 because uv installs are most reliable on modern Mac/Linux; the resolved path is persisted so every later step uses the interpreter that actually has graphify.

nodes.label: Step 2 — Detect Files
nodes.rationale: Detection JSON is read silently and summarised rather than printed; oversized corpora (>2M words or >500 files) trigger a narrowing prompt, and skipped_sensitive is listed so a wrongly-flagged source is visible (#2106).

nodes.label: Step 2.5 — Video and Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are produced first so video/audio can be treated as ordinary doc files by semantic extraction.

nodes.label: Step 3 — Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: AST (Part A) and semantic (Part B) run in parallel because they operate on disjoint file types; parallelising saves 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: Part A — Structural (AST) Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — no LLM and no API key, which is why a code-only corpus needs no semantic pass at all.

nodes.label: Part B — Semantic Extraction (subagents)
nodes.rationale: A code-only corpus still writes an empty .graphify_semantic.json because Part C reads it unconditionally and would otherwise hit FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Part C — Merge AST + Semantic
nodes.rationale: AST nodes are kept first and semantic nodes deduplicated by id, so deterministic structural results win over LLM output on collision.

nodes.label: Step B0 — Check Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Only document/paper/image files are checked — flattening every category would make subagents re-read every source file already covered by AST (#1392). The stale cached file is deleted when there are no hits so Part C never merges leftovers.

nodes.label: Step B1 — Split into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunks of 20-25 files group same-directory files together so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted; each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context.

nodes.label: Step B2 — Dispatch Subagents and Paste Responses
nodes.rationale: This host has no parallel Agent/Task API, so each chunk's subagent is dispatched by hand and its JSON pasted into its own chunk file for Step B3.

nodes.label: Step B3 — Collect, Cache, and Merge
nodes.rationale: Existence of the chunk file on disk is the success signal; a missing file means the subagent was likely read-only and must be warned about, never silently skipped. Real token counts are written back from the Agent usage field because chunk JSON carries placeholder zeros.

nodes.label: Step 4 — Build, Cluster, Analyze, Generate Outputs
nodes.rationale: Empty-graph guard fires before any write so a failed extraction cannot clobber a good graph.json/report; export runs first and the report is written only when the graph was actually written (#1392).

nodes.label: Step 4.5 — Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts: it surfaces the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches — dangling/missing endpoints, self-loops, collapsed edges — so the integrity issue is visible per the Honesty Rules.

nodes.label: Step 5 — Label Communities
nodes.rationale: Questions are regenerated with the real labels because labels affect question phrasing, and graph.json is re-exported so nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490).

nodes.label: Step 6 — Obsidian Vault (opt-in) + HTML
nodes.rationale: HTML is always generated unless --no-viz; the Obsidian vault is opt-in because it writes one file per node.

nodes.label: Step 9 — Save Manifest, Update Cost Tracker, Clean Up
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped, so a failed chunk stays unstamped and is re-queued next --update instead of being marked done and lost (#2015); manifest keys are relativized to the scan root for portability across clones (#1417).

nodes.label: No-API-Key Policy
nodes.rationale: graphify reads no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY at all; when no Gemini key is set the host agent itself is the LLM, so prompting for or blocking on a key is explicitly a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Extraction Backend
nodes.rationale: Used only when GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, replacing subagent dispatch; model defaults to gemini-3-flash-preview and is overridable via GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: Commit Hook and native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.source_location: ## For the commit hook and native CLAUDE.md integration

nodes.label: Post-Pipeline Guided Exploration
nodes.rationale: Only God Nodes, Surprising Connections, and Suggested Questions are pasted, then the single most boundary-crossing question is offered, so the session feels like navigation rather than a one-shot report.

nodes.label: Step 1 — Ensure graphify Is Installed (PowerShell)
nodes.rationale: Resolved interpreter is written to graphify-out/.graphify_python with -NoNewline so subsequent Get-Content invocations yield a clean executable path.

nodes.label: Find-GraphifyPython
nodes.rationale: Probes uv tool dir, then pipx PIPX_LOCAL_VENVS, then the active venv/conda python — 'uv tool dir' and 'pipx environment' are authoritative because they respect UV_TOOL_DIR/PIPX_HOME automatically (fixes #831).

nodes.label: Step B2 — Dispatch ALL Subagents in a Single Message
nodes.rationale: All Agent calls must be in one response or they run sequentially and defeat the purpose; subagent_type must be general-purpose because Explore is read-only and cannot write chunk files, silently dropping results.

nodes.label: graphify.detect.save_manifest
nodes.rationale: scan_corpus is passed the RAW full corpus so newly excluded in-root files are dropped rather than masquerading as deletions (#1908).

nodes.label: graphify.build.build_from_json
nodes.rationale: root= must mirror the --update runbook so source_file is relativized to the same base and full builds never drift from incremental re-extracts (#1361); directed= selects DiGraph vs Graph.

nodes.label: graphify.export.to_json
nodes.rationale: Returns False and writes nothing when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json — the #479 shrink guard.

nodes.label: graphify.cache.save_semantic_cache
nodes.rationale: Must receive the same prompt_file as the read; a write under a different prompt lands where the next run will not look (#1939).

nodes.label: graphify.cli._stamped_manifest_files
nodes.rationale: Code files are always stamped because AST is deterministic; only semantic types are gated on having actually produced output.

nodes.label: graphify-out/.graphify_python
nodes.rationale: Persists the resolved interpreter across invocations so every step and subcommand uses the Python that actually has graphify.

nodes.label: graphify-out/.graphify_root
nodes.rationale: Saves the scan root so a later bare `graphify update` knows where to look.

nodes.label: graphify-out/.graphify_labels.json
nodes.rationale: Must survive until any --wiki export runs, which is why Step 9 cleanup comes after Steps 6b-8.

nodes.label: graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json
nodes.rationale: Written under the project cwd (not .graphify_root) because that is where Part C globs (#1392); its presence on disk is the subagent success signal.

nodes.label: graphify-out/cost.json
nodes.rationale: Cumulative token tracker appended per run, supporting the Honesty Rule that token cost is always shown.

nodes.label: references/extraction-spec.md
nodes.rationale: Doubles as the cache key (SPEC_PATH): entries are attributed to the prompt that produced them, so a prompt change on upgrade forces re-extraction instead of replaying stale results (#1939).

nodes.label: references/exports.md
nodes.rationale: Holds the flag-gated exports (wiki, Neo4j, FalkorDB, SVG, GraphML, MCP, benchmark) so a default run skips all of them.

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: Falls back to inline NetworkX traversal of graph.json when the CLI is unavailable; answers must cite source_location and use only what the graph output contains.

nodes.label: graphify export html
nodes.rationale: Auto-aggregates to a community view above 5,000 nodes, matching the Honesty Rule against unwarned large-graph rendering.

nodes.label: Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: Refuses to overwrite graph.json with a smaller graph so an accidental partial extraction cannot destroy a complete one; overriding requires an explicit --force full build.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Every edge carries its provenance so the graph stays honest; uncertain edges are marked AMBIGUOUS rather than invented or dropped.

nodes.label: --mode deep
nodes.rationale: Must be tracked from the original invocation and passed as DEEP_MODE=true to every subagent, otherwise the richer INFERRED extraction is silently lost.

nodes.label: --directed (IS_DIRECTED)
nodes.rationale: Substituted into build_from_json and diagnose_extraction alike; the literal placeholder must never be left in the code.
